title: Implement burn-rate alert rules + tier-aware notification routing (Hosted vs Dedicated)
creator: Rafael Mendes
project: Tiered SLO definitions + error budget policy
description:
Goal
Ship Redwood-standard burn-rate alerts for tiered SLOs (Hosted API + Dedicated) and route notifications to the correct Slack/PagerDuty targets with consistent annotations/runbook links.

Scope
- Burn-rate alert rules (multi-window) for key SLIs:
  - Hosted: request success/availability (5xx+timeout), streaming disconnect rate, p95 latency (non-streaming) + TTFT (streaming)
  - Dedicated: request success/availability, pool readiness SLI (as available), p95 latency (customer-scoped where possible)
- Alert metadata standards:
  - Required annotations: owner/team, tier, SLO name, runbook URL, dashboard URL, gate impact (warn-only/soft-block/hard-block), escalation policy
  - Required labels: service, tier, region, route_group (coarse), model_family (coarse; see cardinality budget)
- Notification routing:
  - Always notify #eng-sre for burn alerts (visibility + coordination)
  - Page the correct oncall based on tier:
    - Hosted -> platform-oncall
    - Dedicated -> dedicated-oncall
  - Secondary notification: create ticket (non-page) for slow burn / budget-at-risk conditions

Non-goals
- Changing commercial SLAs
- Full Private deployment alerting enforcement (documented separately)

References
- Confluence: Observability standards → Error budget burn-rate alerting standard
- Confluence: Runbook → Error budget exhaustion response
- Initiative docs: Tiered SLO definitions + error budget policy

Acceptance criteria
1) For each in-scope SLO, we have at least:
   - fast-burn page ("page now")
   - medium-burn page OR ticket (tier-dependent)
   - slow-burn ticket ("budget at risk")
2) Alerts include working runbook + dashboard links and specify tier + SLO window.
3) Alertmanager routing verified end-to-end in staging and prod (test alert proves correct Slack + PD target).
4) Alert volume is bounded (anti-flap and grouping); initial tuning documented.

Implementation notes / proposed thresholds (initial)
- Use standard multi-window burn alerts to catch both spikes and sustained degradation.
- Hosted (more sensitive due to multi-tenant blast radius):
  - Page: burn_rate_5m_1h > 14 OR burn_rate_30m_6h > 6
  - Ticket: burn_rate_2h_1d > 3
- Dedicated (avoid paging on brief noisy blips; focus on sustained customer impact):
  - Page: burn_rate_30m_6h > 6
  - Ticket: burn_rate_2h_1d > 3
- Anti-flap:
  - Require 2 consecutive evaluations before firing for latency-based alerts
  - Group by (tier, region, route_group, service) and avoid per-model paging

Deliverables
- Alert rule templates + recording rules in observability-pack
- Alertmanager/PagerDuty routing config in redwood (or infra repo depending on current ownership)
- Documentation: how to interpret burn alerts + where to find dashboards

Owners / collaborators
- DRI: Sergio Costa
- Standards review: Allison Grant
- SRE review: Rafael Mendes, Aisha Bello
- Oncall schedule/routing: Miles Thornton + Internal IT (INT-1188)

Linked work
- GitHub: observability-pack PR #77 (dashboards + alert templates)
- GitHub: redwood PR #18489 (structured alert payloads + runbook links)
- GitHub: redwood PR #18571 (tier-aware alert routing)

Open questions
- Do we page on Dedicated pool readiness dips immediately, or ticket-only until the SLI is stable? (initial recommendation: ticket-only for 2 weeks; promote to page after validation)
- How do we classify streaming disconnects for paging (client abort vs server fault)? (blocker depends on ENG-2428 instrumentation finalization)
